rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes hatta to introduce a conditional-consequential clause and mark the endpoint of Noah's ark-building, which continued until the appointed time.
rows.anchor: هي التي يبتدأ بعدها الكلام أدخلت على الجملة من الشرط والجزاء ووقعت غاية لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr Allah may mean that nothing occurs except by God's command, as in 16:40, or the punishment that had been promised.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى بين أنه لا يحدث شيء إلا بأمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Mujahid identify the tanur as a bread-baking oven.
rows.anchor: فهو قول جماعة عظيمة من المفسرين كابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the oven belonged to Noah, while another view says it had belonged to Adam.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من قال : إنه تنور لنوح عليه السلام ، وقيل : كان لآدم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it was a stone oven belonging to Eve that eventually came to Noah.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : كان تنورا من حجارة ، وكان لحواء حتى صار لنوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī locates Noah's oven in the region of Kufa.
rows.anchor: فقا الشعبي : إنه كان بناحية الكوفة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali locates it in Kufa's mosque and says seventy prophets prayed there.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه في مسجد الكوفة ، قال : وقد صلى فيه سبعون نبيا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil places the oven in Syria at a place called ʿAyn Wardan.
rows.anchor: وقيل بالشام بموضع يقال له : عين وردان وهو قول مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports place the oven in India or say Noah's wife was baking when water emerged from it, prompting him to load the ark immediately.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فار التنور بالهند ، وقيل : إن امرأته كانت تخبز في ذلك التنور فأخبرته بخروج الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A non-oven interpretation takes tanur as the earth's surface, from which water burst forth; the cited flood passage describes water pouring from heaven and springs from earth.
rows.anchor: أنه انفجر الماء من وجه الأرض كما قال : { ففتحنا أبواب السماء بماء منهمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands the tanur as the earth's highest place, where water emerged as a miracle; its height is likened to ovens.
rows.anchor: أن التنور أشرف موضع في الأرض وأعلى مكان فيها وقد أخرج إليه الماء من ذلك الموضع ليكون ذلك معجزة له

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali is reported to interpret the tanur's bursting as the appearance of dawn.
rows.anchor: الثالث : { وفار التنور } أي طلع الصبح وهو منقول عن علي رضي الله عنه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation makes the tanur a figure for an emergency becoming intense: when danger and water rise, Noah should escape with his people to the ark.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون معناه أشد الأمر كما يقال : حمي الوطيس ومعنى الآية إذا رأيت الأمر يشتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the literal bread oven because that is the word's basic sense and it is rationally possible that water first sprang from a particular oven.
rows.anchor: الأصل حمل الكلام على حقيقته ولفظ التنور حقيقة في الموضع الذي يخبز فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the definite article presupposes a known oven, so the phrase must mean that water grew forceful; Razi answers that Noah could have known a specific oven belonging to Adam or Eve, or designated by God as a sign.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يقال : إن ذلك التنور كان لنوح عليه السلام بأن كان تنور آدم أو حواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fara means to gush powerfully, by analogy with a pot boiling over a strong fire; the water, rather than the oven itself, gushed out.
rows.anchor: نبع على قوة وشدة تشبيها بغليان القدر عند قوة النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that the oven's overflow signaled the people's destruction is plausible: a promised deliverance required believers to receive a sign of its appointed time.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع لأن هذه واقعة عظيمة ، وقد وعد الله تعالى المؤمنين النجاة فلا بد وأن يجعل لهم علامة

rows.speaker: ليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says tanur is a word shared across languages and calls its owner tanar.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : التنور لفظة عمت بكل لسان وصاحبه تنار

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari infers that tanur may be a foreign word Arabized, since its original form was tanar and tanur was not previously known in Arabic; he compares other Persian loanwords that became Arabic through use.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري : وهذا يدل على أن الاسم قد يكون أعجميا فتعربه العرب فيصير عربيا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says two individuals can be called a pair and that one individual can also be called a pair; the verse's examples include pairs among creation and human spouses.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش : تقول الاثنان هما زوجان قال تعالى : { ومن كل شىء خلقنا زوجين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's reference to eight pairs among sheep, goats, camels, and cattle also supports using pair terminology for individual male and female animals.
rows.anchor: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين * ومن الإبل اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two members of each pair are a male and a female, so Noah was to take one of each sex of every kind; on Hafs's reading, tanwin on min kullin marks taking two from every kind.
rows.anchor: الزوجان عبارة عن كل شيئين يكون أحدهما ذكرا والآخر أنثى

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads min kullin with tanwin, yielding the sense of two from every kind, one male and one female.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قرأ حفص { من كل } بالتنوين وأرادوا حمل من كل شيء زوجين اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent redundancy in zawjayn ithnayn is answered by parallels such as two gods and one blast; Razi says the objection does not arise on the common reading.
rows.anchor: هذا على مثال قوله : { لا تتخذوا إلاهين اثنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All animals are included in the command; the wording does not itself establish that plants are included, though the practical need for plants makes their inclusion contextually plausible.
rows.anchor: أما الحيوان فداخل لأن قوله : { من كل زوجين اثنين } يدخل فيه كل الحيوانات ، وأما النبات فاللفظ لا يدل عليه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says Noah could not load the lion until God gave it fever after Noah asked how he would feed it; Razi calls such stories best left aside, since an elephant needs even more food and has no fever.
rows.anchor: وجاء في الروايات عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : لم يستطع نوح عليه السلام أن يحمل الأسد حتى ألقيت عليه الحمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark's people are said to have numbered seven—Noah, his three sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives—or eight if Noah's wife is included.
rows.anchor: قالوا : كانوا سبعة نوح عليه السلام وثلاثة أبناء له وهم سام وحام ويافث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those excluded by the prior decree are Noah's son and wife, who were unbelievers and sentenced to destruction.
rows.anchor: فالمراد ابنه وامرأته وكانا كافرين ، حكم الله تعالى عليهم بالهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals are mentioned before humans because rational humans are naturally compelled to protect themselves from destruction, whereas saving other animals requires greater encouragement.
rows.anchor: الإنسان عاقل وهو لعقله كالمضطر إلى دفع أسباب الهلاك عن نفسه

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's theological school uses the prior decree to prove binding predestination: whoever has been decreed for a state cannot depart from it, as in the Prophetic saying that felicity or misery is fixed in the womb.
rows.anchor: احتجوا بقوله : { إلا من سبق عليه القول } في إثبات القضاء اللازم والقدر الواجب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The believers are said to have numbered eighty; Muqatil says a village near Mosul was called the Village of Eighty because the survivors built it after leaving the ark.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : في ناحية الموصل قرية يقال لها قرية الثمانين سميت بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports give higher and lower totals, but their number cannot be known; the Qur'an only characterizes them as few.
rows.anchor: وذكروا ماهو أزيد منه وما هو أنقص منه وذلك مما لا سبيل إلى معرفته إلا أن الله تعالى وصفهم بالقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both qalil and qalilun are valid; here the intended construction is a small number of people, so a singular adjective is permissible with the plural sense.
rows.anchor: كلا اللفظين جائز ، والتقدير ههنا وما آمن معه إلا نفر قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Iblis boarded is remote: as a jinn of fiery or airy substance he would not be affected by drowning, and neither the Qur'an nor a sound report supports it, so Razi advises leaving it aside.
rows.anchor: وأيضا كتاب الله تعالى لم يدل عليه وخبر صحيح ما ورد فيه ، فالأولى ترك الخوض فيه

none: The segment contains only the verse text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible grammatical governors of bi-smi Allah are ride in God's name, begin in God's name, or the statement that its sailing and anchoring are in God's name.
rows.anchor: ذكروا في عامل الإعراب في { بسم الله } وجوها : الأول : اركبوا بسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say the ark set sail on the first of Rajab or after ten days of Rajab, floated for six months, and came to rest on al-Judi on the tenth of Muharram.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنها سارت لأول يوم من رجب ، وقيل : لعشر مضين من رجب ، فصارت ستة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one construction, Noah's command and the invocation form one sentence: boarding should begin with God's sacred name, so that remembrance at the start of every undertaking brings its completion through blessing.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : وقال اركبوا فيها بسم مجريها ومرساها ، يعني ينبغي أن يكون الركوب مقرونا بهذا الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a second construction there are two sentences: Noah orders boarding, then teaches that only God's name, command, and power make the ark sail and anchor; salvation comes through God's grace, not reliance on the boat.
rows.anchor: أن مجريها ومرساها ليس إلا بسم الله وأمره وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first construction places Noah in remembrance when boarding; the second places him in contemplation, disavowing independent power and created means while absorbed in the light of the Cause of causes.
rows.anchor: فعلى التقدير الأول كان نوح عليه السلام وقت ركوب السفينة في مقام الذكر ، وعلى التقدير الثاني كان في مقام الفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi allegorizes the seeker of knowledge as sailing in a ship of reflection through waves of error; the heart and intellect must rely on God until the ship reaches the shore of salvation.
rows.anchor: إذا ابتدأت سفينة الفكرة والروية بالحركة وجب أن يكون هناك اعتماده على الله تعالى وتضرعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi transmits from Ibn Abbas that God punished no two communities with the same punishment except the peoples of Shuayb and Salih: Salih's people were struck by a cry from below, Shuayb's from above.
rows.anchor: روى الكلبي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : لم يعذب الله تعالى أمتين بعذاب واحد إلا قوم شعيب وقوم صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrival of God's command may mean the time when He commanded an angel to make the cry, or may mean the punishment itself.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد منه ولما جاء وقت أمرنا ملكا من الملائكة بتلك الصيحة ، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد من الأمر العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb's rescue by mercy may mean that salvation came purely by divine mercy, showing that all a servant receives is God's grace, or that mercy means faith, obedience, and righteous works, themselves granted by God's enabling.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى إنما خلصه من ذلك العذاب لمحض رحمته ، تنبيها على أن كل ما يصل إلى العبد فليس إلا بفضل الله ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-sayha points to the already-known cry, identified as Gabriel's cry.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر الصيحة بالألف واللام إشارة إلى المعهود السابق وهي صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jathimin means remaining fixed in place without moving; Gabriel's cry killed each person where he was, as if they had never lived and moved in their homes.
rows.anchor: والجاثم الملازم لمكانه الذي لا يتحول عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse and distance from Midian are compared with Thamud because God punished them in the same manner.
rows.anchor: وإنما قاس حالهم على ثمود لما ذكرنا أنه تعالى عذبهم مثل عذاب ثمود .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayat covers both signs that yield probability and proofs that yield certainty; sultan denotes proof yielding certainty, whether sensory-confirmed or not, while a clear sultan is a decisive proof confirmed by sense.
rows.anchor: الآيات اسم للقدر المشترك بين العلامات التي تفيد الظن ، وبين الدلائل التي تفيد اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' miracles were decisive proofs confirmed by sense, which is why God calls them a clear authority.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت معجزات موسى عليه السلام هكذا لا جرم وصفها الله بأنها سلطان مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to Pharaoh and his chiefs means that Moses was sent to Pharaoh and his company.
rows.anchor: يعني وأرسلنا موسى بآياتنا بمثل هذه الآيات إلى فرعون وملائه ، أي جماعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Pharaoh's command may mean obeying his instruction to disbelieve Moses and his miracles, or following his path and way of life.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد أمره إياهم بالكفر بموسى ومعجزاته ويحتمل أن يكون المراد من الأمر الطريق والشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rashid can mean guiding toward good, or possessing sound judgment.
rows.anchor: أي بمرشد إلى خير ، وقيل رشيد أي ذي رشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh wholly lacked right guidance because he denied a Creator and resurrection, claimed the world had no god, urged worship of each local ruler for social utility, and denied that knowing and worshipping God is guidance.
rows.anchor: كان دهريا نافيا للصانع والمعاد وكان يقول : لا إله للعالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistically, qaddama means to advance before someone; Razi illustrates it with the forepart of a foot and the vanguard of an army.
rows.anchor: يقال : قدم فلان فلانا بمعنى تقدمه ، ومنه قادمة الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh led his people in worldly misguidance and will lead them into the Fire, where they follow; alternatively, as he led them into the sea and drowned them, he now advances ahead into the Fire.
rows.anchor: فرعون كان قدوة لقومه في الضلال حال ما كانوا في الدنيا وكذلك مقدمهم إلى النار وهم يتبعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rashid may mean a sound, praiseworthy outcome; the next statement that Pharaoh leads his people into the Fire explains why his course cannot be rightly guided.
rows.anchor: وما أمره بصالح حميد العاقبة ويكون قوله : { يقدم قومه } تفسيرا لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future is expressed with the past fa-awrada because a completed past event cannot be averted; this phrasing emphatically presents the future outcome as certain.
rows.anchor: لأن الماضي قد وقع ودخل في الوجود فلا سبيل ألبتة إلى دفعه

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Although nar is feminine, the noun wird is masculine, so both masculine and feminine agreement are allowed; al-Wahidi gives the analogous constructions ni'ma al-manzil and ni'mat al-manzil.
rows.anchor: إلا أن لفظ ( الورد ) مذكر ، فكان التذكير والتأنيث جائزين كما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wird can mean the act of arriving, the one who arrives (as in 19:86), or the destination where water is reached; al-Zamakhshari calls it an arrival that has actually taken place.
rows.anchor: الورد قد يكون بمعنى الورود فيكون مصدرا وقد يكون بمعنى الوارد

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says al-wird al-mawrud means an arrival that has been made.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الورد المورود الذي حصل وروده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image makes Pharaoh the leader of those arriving at water and his followers the arrivals, but their destination is the Fire, the opposite of water that quenches thirst and cools hearts.
rows.anchor: فشبه الله تعالى فرعون بمن يتقدم الواردة إلى الماء وشبه أتباعه بالواردين إلى الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were followed by a curse both in this life and on Judgment Day; the curse of God, angels, and prophets remains attached to them, as also stated in 28:42.
rows.anchor: أن اللعن من الله ومن الملائكة والأنبياء ملتصق بهم في الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا يزول عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafd means a gift and originally denotes assistance toward an objective; the condemned received a wretched added provision.
rows.anchor: والرفد هو العطية وأصله الذي يعين على المطلوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Nafi ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas about the wretched added provision, Ibn Abbas said it is curse upon curse.
rows.anchor: سأل نافع بن الأزرق ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن قوله : { بئس الرفد المرفود } قال هو اللعنة بعد اللعنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says two curses from God accumulated on them, one in this world and one in the next; anything made an aid to another has been rafad to it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : ترادفت عليهم لعنتان من الله تعالى لعنة في الدنيا ولعنة في الآخرة

none: The segment contains only Qur'an verse text, with no commentary.
The segment contains only Qur'an verse text, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After giving every argument, warning, encouragement, and threat, God tells the unaffected disbelievers to act as they can while the believers act; the meaning is to do all they can to harm the Prophet and his followers, who will also act.
rows.anchor: اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون } وهذا عين ما حكاه الله تعالى عن شعيب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased as an imperative, act is a threat, as in the commands to Satan and the permission to believe or disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { اعملوا } وإن كانت صيغته صيغة الأمر ، إلا أن المراد منها التهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers await Satan's promise of abandonment, while the believers await the Merciful's promise of forgiveness and generosity.
rows.anchor: وانتظروا ما يعدكم الشيطان من الخذلان فإنا منتظرون ما وعدنا الرحمن من أنواع الغفران والإحسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses wait as awaiting destruction, while the believers await the punishment coming to the opponents.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : { وانتظروا } الهلاك فإنا منتظرون لكم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human knowledge concerns three things: past, present, and future; regarding the past, one must know the prior existent that brought the human from nonexistence into existence, namely God.
rows.anchor: مجموع مايحتاج الإنسان إلى معرفته أمور ثلاثة . وهي : الماضي والحاضر والمستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's essence and the reality of His identity are wholly unknowable to humans; they know only His attributes, divided into attributes of majesty and attributes of generosity.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن حقيقة ذات الإله وكنه هويته غير معلومة للبشر ألبتة ، وإنما المعلوم للبشر صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributes of majesty are negations and are not perfection in themselves, since negation is sheer absence; God's being free of sleep signifies perfection only because it indicates enduring, comprehensive knowledge, unlike a corpse or inanimate object that also does not sleep.
rows.anchor: وهذه السلوب في الحقيقة ليست صفات الكمال ، لأن السلوب عدم ، والعدم المحض والنفي الصرف ، لا كمال فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God feeds but is not fed signifies His majesty because He exists necessarily in Himself and needs no food, drink, or anything else.
rows.anchor: يفيد كونه واجب الوجود لذاته غنيا عن الطعام والشراب بل عن كل ما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perfection, might, and exaltedness are positive attributes; the most exalted positive attributes are knowledge and power, which the verse names in praise of God.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن صفات الكمال والعز والعلو هي الصفات الثبوتية ، وأشرف الصفات الثبوتية الدالة على الكمال والجلال صفتان : العلم والقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge reaches every universal and particular, existent and nonexistent, present and absent; Razi refers to his explanation of the proof in 6:59.
rows.anchor: والمراد أن علمه نافذ في جميع الكليات والجزئيات والمعدومات والموجودات والحاضرات والغائبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return of every affair to God demonstrates His power: He is the source of all and the destination of all originated, contingent things.
rows.anchor: والمراد أن مرجع الكل إليه ، وإنما يكون كذلك لو كان مصدر الكل ومبدأ الكل هو هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power is sovereign over nonexistence, bringing things into existence and carrying them from potentiality to actuality and completion.
rows.anchor: كان عظيم القدرة نافذ المشيئة قهارا للعدم بالوجود والتحصيل جبارا له بالقوة والفعل والتكميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second essential rank of knowledge is what matters during worldly life: perfecting the soul through spiritual knowledge and sacred illuminations, a path with a beginning and an end.
rows.anchor: أن يعرف ما هو مهم له في زمان حياته في الدنيا ، وما ذلك إلا تكميل النفس بالمعارف الروحانية والجلايا القدسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beginning of this rank is bodily and spiritual worship; among bodily acts, prayer is the best movement, fasting the most complete stillness, and charity the most beneficial good deed.
rows.anchor: أما العبادات الجسدانية ، فأفضل الحركات الصلاة ، وأكمل السكنات الصيام ، وأنفع البر الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual worship is reflection on the wonders of God's creation in the heavens and earth, as in 3:191.
rows.anchor: وأما العبادة الروحانية فهي : الفكر ، والتأمل في عجائب صنع الله تعالى في ملكوت السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The end of the path is leaving created causes for their Cause, turning reason toward the light of majesty, and the spirit toward divine glory until all else is seen as fleeting before God.
rows.anchor: فالانتهاء من الأسباب إلى مسببها ، وقطع النظر عن كل الممكنات والمبدعات ، وتوجيه حدقة العقل إلى نور عالم الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first station on the way to God is worship and the last is reliance on God, which explains the command to worship and trust in Him.
rows.anchor: أن أول درجات السير إلى الله تعالى هو عبودية الله ، وآخرها التوكل على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third essential rank is knowledge of the future: what follows bodily life and whether deeds affect happiness or misery, signaled by God's not being unaware of people's actions.
rows.anchor: والمرتبة الثالثة : من المراتب المهمة لكل عامل معرفة المستقبل وهو أنه يعرف كيف يصير حاله بعد انقضاء هذه الحياة الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither loses the obedient person's good deeds nor overlooks the rebellious; all will be resurrected and judged for even the smallest and greatest acts.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يضيع طاعات المطيعين ولا يهمل أحوال المتمردين الجاحدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final outcome is one group in Paradise and one in the Fire; Razi says this verse encompasses all exalted aims and leaves reason and thought nowhere further to ascend.
rows.anchor: ثم يحصل عاقبة الأمر فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير ، فظهر أن هذه الآية وافية بالإشارة إلى جميع المطالب العلوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The colophon says Razi completed the surah's commentary before dawn on Monday in Rajab 601; grieving his deceased young son, he asks readers to pray for the son and for him, ending with a prayer from 3:8.
rows.anchor: وقد كان لي ولد صالح حسن السيرة فتوفى في الغربة في عنفوان شبابه ، وكان قلبي كالمحترق لذلك السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heading identifies Surah Yusuf as Meccan except for verses 1, 2, 3, and 7, which are Medinan; it has 111 verses and was revealed after Hud.
rows.anchor: مكية ، إلا الآيات : 1 و 2 و 3 و 7 ، فمدنية
